column3: Warm evening, a tiny clay cinema ticket booth on a Vietnamese street corner: sage-green clay awning with a row of glowing warm bulbs, terracotta flower pots. Hun stands behind the booth counter hugging one big pink clay movie ticket (notched edges, no text) against its belly, smiling. The centre of the frame is calm and soft (a panel of text will sit over it). No text anywhere.

Blue dusk on the front step of the clay house: a sage-green clay mailbox, a string of warm fairy lights along the doorway, potted plants. Hun sits on the step holding a small cream clay envelope against its belly, reading it, curious; a small pile of envelopes beside. Keep the centre calm. No text anywhere.

A small clay theatre stage, heavy sage-green clay curtains half closed from both sides, a warm spotlight circle on the stage floor; Hun stands in the spotlight taking a polite little bow (short flippers out to the sides), a few pink clay petals on the floor; the fish jar full of tiny orange clay fish sits at the edge of the stage. Dark soft background. No text.
